note_sections.t: Specialist assessment required after confirmed malignancy and subsequent PSA elevation.

A 73-year-old warehouse manager seeks specialist guidance following prolonged urological tracking. He is married and resides in an independent unit within a retirement community. He is a non-smoker. Lower urinary tract complaints remain minimal, yielding a 4/35 IPSS score. Despite significant anxiety surrounding invasive diagnostics, he requests thorough consultations. His medical history contains no comorbidities, and he takes no active medication, aside from a minor knee arthroscopy more than ten years ago and a recent dermatology check for actinic keratosis monitoring. He explicitly denies bone discomfort, unexplained weight reduction, or blood in the urine.

DRE — texture: firm; mobility: fixed; asymmetry: palpable nodus in the right lobe. The remaining abdominal and cardiovascular survey shows no anomalies. Vital signs record 111/74 mmHg with a steady pulse of 72 bpm. He demonstrates adequate perfusion and preserves standard functional capacity.

admin: Patient anxious about procedures — allocate extra consult time.
